sentences.text: Corynebacterium matruchotii is a bacterium of the human mouth that is usually isolated from dental calculus.
It is a confirmed calcifying organism that can induce mineralisation in vitro, and calcium ions are required for the needle- and plate-like crystals that form inside its cells.
Using in situ hybridization probes and sequencing, researchers described a central pillar role for this species in supragingival plaque, with a biofilm structure dominated by it.
Laboratory work has measured its uptake of inorganic phosphate, part of a microbially mediated ion exchange that alters the mineral saturation state of surface enamel.
A review reports that it appears to be an indicator of caries-free oral status in imaging and sequencing studies.
